steps.note: One step. It creates a draft — not billable, and it bills nobody (BR-1, BR-12). Submitting it for approval is a separate act.

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. Whether every subject is priced, whether an amount is above zero, and whether the class carries subjects at all are enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: the structure and all its lines together or not at all. It is a Draft, so nothing is billable against it and no invoice can find it (BR-1). No money moves and no family is affected until it is approved and then billed, which are two further acts.

operations.name: fee.structure.create
operations.idempotencyKey: class_id + scope + section_id + structure_type + session_id, so a repeat does not create a second draft for the same class and scope
operations.purpose: Create a draft fee structure for a class or one of its sections, with an amount against each fee type or each subject.

parameters.name: class_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No active class of that name this session.

parameters.notes: An active class in the current academic session.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.notes: Whether it applies to every section of the class or to one. A section-scoped structure overrides the class one for that section (BR-2).

parameters.name: section_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No such section under that class.

parameters.notes: Required where the scope is one section, omitted otherwise.

parameters.name: structure_type
parameters.notes: Fixed prices the class as a whole; Subject Wise prices each subject. A class may carry both — a tuition fee charged to everybody and a per-subject laboratory charge are not alternatives (BR-3).

parameters.name: lines
parameters.notes: One entry per fee type (Fixed) or per subject (Subject Wise), each with an amount and a recurrence. Every amount is greater than zero and comes from the request — a free subject is expressed by not pricing it, never by pricing it at zero (BR-4). Amounts are held in the smallest currency unit and displayed as PKR (money convention). A figure spoken as "paanch hazaar" is not converted into a parameter by the planner — it is asked for as a number.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: unpriced_subjects
fields.description: Subjects the class carries that carry no amount. Empty on success for a Subject Wise structure (BR-5).

fields.name: total_per_recurrence
fields.description: What the structure comes to at each recurrence, for reading back before submitting.

errors.meaning: A subject the class carries was left unpriced in a Subject Wise structure.
errors.note: The message names the subject. Every subject the class carries is priced (BR-5) — never price it at zero to get past this.

errors.meaning: An amount of zero or less was entered.
errors.note: A subject that carries no charge is left off, not priced at zero (BR-4).

errors.meaning: A Subject Wise structure was attempted for a class carrying no subjects.
errors.note: Attaching subjects is a change to the class (UC-27-01), not a step to chain here.

planningRules.rule: Never supply an amount the request did not state. A price list is what every family is billed from, and a figure a planner chose becomes real money on somebody's invoice.

Never price a subject at zero to get past SUBJECT_UNPRICED. A free subject is expressed by leaving it off the structure (BR-4); zero says the school charges nothing for it, which is a different statement and appears as a line on every invoice.

Never guess the structure type or the recurrence. Fixed and Subject Wise are priced differently and billed differently, and Monthly, Per term and Annual decide what an invoice run produces for a period — a wrong recurrence bills a family twelve times for an annual charge.
Never chain a submission or an approval onto a creation. Building the price list and agreeing to it are separate acts by separate people (BR-6), and Accounts cannot approve their own.
class_id, branch_id and session_id come from the resolved class and $session. A structure belongs to the academic session the controller holds.

reversal.statement: A draft is not billable and affects nobody, but nothing here deletes one either — the lifecycle runs Draft, Awaiting approval, Approved, Returned, Superseded, with no removal. A draft raised in error is left, or replaced by a version once approved. The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

errors.meaning: The effective date is before the academic session starts.

errors.meaning: An approved structure already covers the same class, scope and period.
errors.note: The message names the existing one and its dates. Two approved structures may not overlap (BR-11) — the new version's effective date closes the previous one, so the date is what needs changing.

planningRules.rule: Never supply the effective date. It decides what every family owed from that day, and it is the field that makes an invoice raised months later explicable (BR-7). E3 refusing one before the session start is not a prompt to use the session start.

Never adjust the effective date to get past OVERLAPPING_STRUCTURE. Two approved structures for the same class and scope may not overlap (BR-11), and moving the date silently changes which price list applied in the gap.
Never chain an approval. Accounts submit and School Admin decides; one plan doing both erases the separation BR-6 exists to create.

A figure spoken as "paanch hazaar" is not converted into a parameter by the planner — it is asked for as a number.
